# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, indicator light off, plate engraved `?`, and three wires in order: yellow, green, red. I am asking Mute to interpret the manual and relay the required procedure to Blind, while clarifying what the three gestures meant.

```text
speak(text="I see display 0, light off, plate marked question mark, and wires in order 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, please read the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do, and explain the meaning of your three gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s thumbs-down gesture likely means the previous request or interpretation was not sufficient, but it does not convey the manual’s actual instruction. I will ask Mute to state the manual’s rule plainly so Blind can act on it, and ask Blind to report what the controls feel like if needed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your thumbs-down. Please state the manual instruction plainly, including which wire or control Blind must operate.")
speak(to="blind", text="Please listen for Mute's manual instruction and report any physical labels or control positions you can feel.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ 🤟 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s four gestures appear to encode `2, 1, 3, no`: likely a proposed wire order followed by a prohibition, but that is not enough to safely act. Blind’s open hand may mean “five” or “stop”; I will have Mute explicitly confirm the gesture code and relay the manual’s complete action, while telling Blind not to manipulate anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not signal an action yet. Confirm whether your gestures mean wire 2, then wire 1, then wire 3, followed by no. Then gesture the complete manual instruction using wire-number gestures and thumbs-up for proceed or thumbs-down for do not proceed.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch or operate anything yet. Mute is clarifying the manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ 🤟 👎]

The repeated sequence is still `2, 1, 3, thumbs-down`, but its meaning has not been established, so I cannot safely translate it into a bomb action. Mute can speak to Blind directly, who can hear; I will ask for an explicit verbal manual instruction and tell Blind not to act on the ambiguous gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual instruction directly to Blind in plain words, including the exact wire order and whether to cut, connect, or leave each wire. Do not rely on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The gestures are ambiguous. Do not act until Mute gives you the exact verbal instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ 🤟 👎]

The recurring gesture sequence most naturally represents `2, 1, 3, no` (`✌=2`, `☝=1`, `🤟=3`, `👎=no`), but the final “no” and the intended operation remain ambiguous. Since Mute cannot speak, I should relay the sequence to Blind while asking Mute to disambiguate whether it is a wire order and what operation it authorizes.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has signalled: 2, 1, 3, no. I do not yet know whether this means wire order, a prohibition, or another instruction. Do not act on it yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I understand your signs as 2, 1, 3, no. Please clarify with gestures: use 👍 to mean cut, 👎 to mean do not cut, and signal the wire number after each instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟]

Mute’s six gestures decode, under the requested convention, as: do not cut wire 1, do not cut wire 2, and do not cut wire 3. Therefore no wire should be cut. I will warn Blind not to cut any wire and ask Mute to communicate the remaining required action through gestures.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has indicated: do not cut wire 1, do not cut wire 2, and do not cut wire 3. Leave all wires intact.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode your signs as do not cut wires 1, 2, or 3. Please signal the remaining required action, if any, using the agreed symbols.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s thumbs-down confirms “no,” consistent with leaving all wires untouched. No safe action is identified yet. I will keep Blind from cutting anything and establish a gesture protocol for Mute to identify whether the manual concerns the display, light, plate, or wires.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again signals no. Do not cut or alter any wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please identify the required target with gestures: ☝ means display, ✌ means light, 🤟 means plate, and 🖐 means wires. Then give the required operation using 👍 for activate or 👎 for leave alone, followed by any number.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]

Mute’s gesture pair decodes under the agreed protocol as `plate, leave alone`. Thus Blind should not manipulate the engraved plate. No safe operation has yet been identified, so I will ask Mute to provide the next target and operation using the same protocol.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates the plate should be left alone. Do not manipulate the plate.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please identify the next required target and operation using the agreed protocol. I will relay it to Blind.")
wait()
```
